title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: MAVIS'S TEAM
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Mavis Odom, a hospital switchboard operator in Kansas City, Missouri.
She knows where every doctor is. But nobody ever asks her anything else.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE INVITE
segments.quote: Action may not always bring happiness; but there is no happiness without action.
segments.author: Benjamin Disraeli
lines: One day, a young mechanic named Jerome heard her shouting crossword answers in the cafeteria.
He said, Our trivia team at Gus's Tavern needs a brain. Tuesday at seven.
Mavis said no. Then her desk calendar quoted the British statesman Benjamin Disraeli:
Action may not always bring happiness; but there is no happiness without action.
Tuesday at seven, she walked into Gus's, holding her purse like a shield.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: SYDNEY
segments.quote: Ignorance more frequently begets confidence than does knowledge.
segments.author: Charles Darwin
lines: By week three, Mavis was answering before the host finished asking.
Capital of Australia? Sydney! Wrong. Canberra. They lost by one point.
Bernice, a retired nurse on the team, quoted Charles Darwin:
Ignorance more frequently begets confidence than does knowledge.
So Mavis learned three new words. I'm not sure.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE LIBRARY
segments.quote: Curiosity is one of the permanent and certain characteristics of a vigorous intellect.
segments.author: Samuel Johnson
lines: She got curious about what she didn't know. Sports. Cars. Any song after nineteen ninety.
At the library, she found Samuel Johnson, the man who wrote a famous English dictionary:
Curiosity is one of the permanent and certain characteristics of a vigorous intellect.
She wrote vigorous intellect on her name tag.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE PHONE
segments.quote: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool.
segments.author: Richard Feynman
lines: By October, they were tied for first. And a rival was reading his phone under the table.
Jerome whispered, We could look stuff up too.
Mavis remembered the physicist Richard Feynman:
The first principle is that you must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool.
She zipped every phone into her purse. Loudly.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE FINAL
segments.quote: No man is wise enough by himself.
segments.author: Plautus
lines: Championship night. Last question. What does a car's alternator do?
Mavis had no idea. Jerome turned red, too shy to speak.
She thought of the old Roman playwright Plautus:
No man is wise enough by himself.
She slid Jerome the pencil. It charges the battery. Correct! Gus dropped a tray.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE TROPHY
segments.quote: I have no special talent. I am only passionately curious.
segments.author: Albert Einstein
lines: The trophy, a plastic gold beer mug, sits on her switchboard, under a note from Albert Einstein:
I have no special talent. I am only passionately curious.
Now the doctors ask her all kinds of questions.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Act. Admit what you don't know. Stay curious. Be honest. Share the pencil.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Act. Say I'm not sure. Stay curious. Don't fool yourself. Share the pencil.
I joined a trivia team once. I knew every answer, a week too late.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
